title: How Does a Turkey Pop-Up Timer Know? 🦃 #shorts
description:
That little plastic button in a Thanksgiving turkey has no battery and no electronics. Inside is a spring-loaded red stick held down by a tiny blob of metal similar to solder. The alloy is chosen to melt at around turkey-done temperature, so when the meat gets hot enough the metal turns liquid, lets go of the stick, and the spring shoots it up. The idea came from a turkey farmer who borrowed it from fire sprinklers, which use a melting metal plug to release water; it was patented in 1961. But timers can pop early, so double-check with a food thermometer: 165°F in the thickest parts.
